summary:
Why we are building it
Astronauts on deep-space missions are far from help, and their bodies change in microgravity. Fluids shift toward the head, sleep suffers, and radiation builds up. The real danger is slow drift that nobody notices until it matters. AURA-TWIN is a digital twin of a crew member that watches for that drift, forecasts risk 72 hours ahead, and explains why.

What makes it different
It senses without touching, using camera pulse and voice fatigue. It compares each body system with the person's own baseline and shows its evidence on screen, so the crew can question every forecast. A what-if simulator lets them test more sleep or hydration before acting, and findings end in a clear SBAR handoff.

Challenges
Sensor accuracy in real cabin conditions, clinical validation of forecasts, onboard processing when Earth is delayed, and privacy. Our answers are a signal quality gate, consent-first capture with no raw video stored, and honest labelling as decision support, not a medical device.

Why it matters
As Artemis missions travel farther, crews must be more self-reliant. AURA-TWIN turns hidden drift into early, explainable, actionable insight. It is already a live, working prototype at aura-twin-olive.vercel.app.
details:
AURA-TWIN: Project Details

What it does

AURA-TWIN gives an astronaut a living digital twin. It reads gentle signals from the camera (pulse) and voice (fatigue), compares each body system with that person's own baseline, and forecasts risk 72 hours ahead. Every forecast shows its evidence, and a what-if simulator lets the crew test choices like extra sleep or hydration before acting.

Benefits

• Catches slow drift before it becomes a medical problem.

• Needs no wearables, so there is nothing for the crew to put on.

• Explains itself, so the crew can question every forecast.

• Ends in an SBAR handoff, so the crew chief gets a clear next step.

Intended impact

As missions travel farther from Earth, crews must rely on themselves. AURA-TWIN turns hidden drift into early, explainable, actionable insight, so crews can act sooner and call for help earlier.

Tools and technology

• Built with Claude Artifacts and deployed on Vercel at aura-twin-olive.vercel.app, with a separate technical-specification site.

• Web technologies (HTML, CSS, JavaScript), with browser camera and microphone input.

• Hardware is a design target only (dual 4K RGB + NIR camera, 8 MEMS microphones, 12.8 TOPS edge processor). It has not been built or tested.

What makes it creative

• One twin, not one health score: each body system is measured against the person's own baseline.

• A what-if simulator for the next 72 hours.

• A decision ladder (Observe, Explain, Prepare, Escalate) instead of a single alarm.

What we considered

• Trust: a signal quality gate lowers confidence when input is weak.

• Privacy: camera analysis is consent-first, and raw video is never stored.

• Honesty: it is a prototype using demo values, not a medical device, and forecasts are not clinically validated.

• Next: secure server-side AI, user accounts, and testing with real sensors and clinical experts.
